Denver's run success rate is 41.8% [mc3] against Pittsburgh's 36.5% [mc4] allowed over 211.0 [mc5] runs, and Denver runs left 35.0% [mc10], middle 30.3% [mc11] and right 34.6% [mc12], so Pittsburgh needs a ready backup who can fit every gap. Third, red-zone finishing: Denver allows touchdowns on 53.1% [mc13] of red-zone drives, but Pittsburgh's offense is at -0.07 [mc15] EPA per pass play over 402.0 [mc16] plays, so it must turn trips into touchdowns rather than field goals. Fourth, the quick game against pressure: Denver sends five or more rushers on 34.3% [mc19] of dropbacks, so Pittsburgh should lean on hot throws to Waddle, who leads targets at 19.9% [mc20].
